title: "RvS: What is Essential for Offline RL via Supervised Learning?"

en.text: Ask most people how to do offline reinforcement learning, learning a policy from a fixed batch of logged data without ever interacting with the environment, and the answer usually starts with value functions: fit a Q-function, then improve the policy against it. Methods built on temporal-difference (TD) learning are powerful in theory, but they are notoriously fiddly in practice, leaning on stabilization tricks and careful hyperparameter tuning to keep from diverging.

An appealing alternative reframes the RL problem as conditional imitation learning. The key insight is that a trajectory that looks terrible for one goal may be an optimal demonstration for another. If you feed the policy an extra input, the outcome you want it to reach, and then simply fit the logged actions with ordinary supervised learning, you can sidestep value functions entirely. But the recipe had been murky. Different papers reached contradictory conclusions about what makes it work: some insisted on advantage weighting, others reached for large Transformer sequence models. Which components are actually essential, and which are just incidental complexity that a practitioner can safely drop?

This ICLR 2022 paper, from UC Berkeley and Carnegie Mellon, does not propose yet another algorithm. Instead it gathers these methods under one framework it calls RvS (Reinforcement Learning via Supervised Learning) and then, through extensive experiments, boils them down to the essentials. The finding is surprising: a plain two-layer feedforward network (an MLP), trained simply to maximize likelihood, matches the state of the art set by far more complex methods built on TD learning or Transformer sequence models. Only two things turn out to decide the outcome: how much capacity the model has, and what you condition on.

en.caption: Figure 1. Across the D4RL Kitchen, Gym, and AntMaze suites, goal-conditioned RvS-G and reward-conditioned RvS-R are compared against prior methods and baselines. Each bar is the average return over many tasks in a suite. Using nothing but supervised learning with a feedforward MLP, RvS matches methods that rely on TD learning and Transformer sequence models.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.10751　　Code: https://github.com/scottemmons/rvs
Why bother stripping the method down

Value-based methods dominate offline and off-policy RL, and they come with attractive theoretical guarantees. In practice, though, they are hard to deploy: they require a stack of tricks to stabilize training and delicate tuning across many hyperparameters. Recasting RL as a conditional, filtered, or weighted imitation-learning problem is tempting precisely because it only asks for supervised learning. If a minimal supervised recipe can match the complex methods, it gives practitioners a dependable field guide, and it also reveals exactly where such methods still break down.

The paper's contributions come in three parts. First, rather than inventing a new algorithm, it places existing goal-conditioned and reward-conditioned methods under the single RvS framework. Second, through large-scale experiments it distills them to their essence, showing that a two-layer MLP trained with maximum likelihood is competitive with much more complex, state-of-the-art methods. Third, it pins down which choices genuinely matter (capacity, regularization, and the conditioning variable) and is honest about the limits: on purely random data, RvS is comparatively weak, a boundary the authors are careful to flag.
RvS: a deliberately simple framework

The setup is plain. An agent lives in a Markov decision process, and we train a policy conditioned on an outcome, π(a | s, ω), where the outcome ω can be a future goal state (giving RvS-G) or the average return over some future window (giving RvS-R). Given a batch of offline trajectories, RvS applies hindsight relabeling to build its training set: every action that actually occurred becomes a demonstration for whatever outcome that trajectory actually reached.

It helps to separate the two flavors of outcome. In RvS-G the outcome is a goal state, so the policy learns to reach configurations of the world; in RvS-R it is an average future return, so the policy learns to hit a level of performance. Hindsight relabeling is what makes both trainable from unlabeled logs: because we read off the outcome each action actually led to, even aimless or suboptimal experience becomes a valid demonstration for some outcome. That is the same insight that lets a trajectory which failed at one task serve as a perfectly good example for another.

en.caption: Figure 2. Hindsight relabeling. States s and actions a from a trajectory are relabeled as demonstrations toward the outcomes ω they actually reached, turning a batch of unfiltered experience into supervised (state + goal → action) data.

en.text: With that dataset in hand, the training objective is nothing more than maximizing the log-likelihood of the observed actions under the conditioned policy: concatenate the outcome ω onto the input state s, and let a two-layer fully connected MLP predict the action. There is no advantage weighting, no TD bootstrapping, and no Transformer, just a maximum-likelihood objective over relabeled experience. At test time you hand the policy the outcome you want (a goal state or a target return) and let it act.
Where it is evaluated

The evaluation is broad, spanning navigation, locomotion, and manipulation. On the D4RL benchmark the authors use three suites: AntMaze (an 8-DoF quadruped navigating a maze), Gym Locomotion (HalfCheetah, Hopper, and Walker, with data quality ranging from random to medium-expert), and Franka Kitchen (a 9-DoF manipulation task built from human demonstrations). They add the GCSL suite of goal-conditioned tasks, including 2D navigation, a Sawyer arm, Lunar Lander, and a robotic claw, adapted to the offline setting with data collected by a random policy. All scores are normalized to the [0, 100] range for comparison.

en.caption: Figure 3. Several goal-conditioned environments from the GCSL suite (left to right: FourRooms navigation, Lunar Lander, the robotic Claw, Door opening, and Pusher). Together with the D4RL locomotion and manipulation tasks, they form a broad sweep from navigation to fine-grained control.

en.text: The result: an MLP reaches state of the art

The headline is striking. Using only a two-layer feedforward network and a maximum-likelihood objective, RvS reaches state-of-the-art performance across several suites. On AntMaze, goal-conditioned RvS-G averages 53.5, edging out the strongest value-based baseline, CQL-p at 50.6. On Kitchen it reaches 54.0. On the GCSL suite it scores 62.0, beating online GCSL at 58.0, and it does so from purely offline, random-policy data. On Gym Locomotion, reward-conditioned RvS-R matches Decision Transformer while using a simple MLP rather than a large Transformer.

The most counterintuitive part concerns subtrajectory stitching. The mixed dataset in Kitchen and all of the AntMaze tasks require assembling fragments of different trajectories, and the field long assumed such tasks demanded dynamic-programming-style value methods. RvS-G keeps pace here too, which suggests that supervised learning is not as inherently incapable of stitching as one might expect. To be fair about the picture: on Gym, value-based methods (such as CQL-r at 63.0) still score higher, so RvS is best read as matching the state of the art with the simplest possible means, not as beating everything outright.

en.caption: Table 1. Normalized average scores per suite (excerpted from the paper's Table 1; scores in [0, 100]).
en.note: Note: the 58.0 in the GCSL row is the online GCSL method. Some baselines marked with * in the paper use AntMaze v0; see Appendix A of the original paper. RvS-G is not run on Gym, which is framed as reward maximization, so that cell is left blank.

en.text: What actually matters: capacity and regularization

Because the model is so simple, its success rests on a handful of design choices, and the ablations nail them down one by one. The first is capacity: the best architectures are larger than those used in standard online RL or imitation learning, and widening the hidden layers up to 1024 units generally keeps helping. The second is regularization: dropout is not universally good. It boosts performance on the small, human-demonstration kitchen-complete dataset, but it hurts on hopper-medium-expert and antmaze-medium-play.

en.caption: Figure 4. Capacity and regularization ablation across four environments, varying network width (x-axis) against dropout (blue = none, orange = p=0.1). Larger networks help on hopper-medium-expert and kitchen-complete, underscoring the value of high-capacity policy networks, while dropout is a reliable win only on small datasets like kitchen-complete.

en.text: One reading is that kitchen-complete is small and drawn from human demonstrations, so it is prone to overfitting and benefits from the extra regularization dropout provides, whereas on tasks with more data (or data that is already close to random) forcing dropout only throttles the policy's capacity. In other words, high-capacity policy networks and just-enough regularization have to be tuned together to get strong results.

The third choice is the policy's output distribution. The paper compares a categorical distribution over a discretized action space against a unimodal Gaussian over continuous actions. Across the GCSL suite, the categorical distribution generally matches or beats the Gaussian, echoing the same theme that more policy capacity helps. There is also a useful caution for anyone tuning these models: validation loss correlates only loosely with final performance, so it is not a reliable signal to tune against in practice.

en.caption: Figure 5. Across four GCSL environments, a categorical distribution over discretized actions (orange) generally matches or exceeds a unimodal Gaussian over continuous actions (blue), consistent with the broader pattern that higher-capacity RvS models perform better.

en.text: A field guide you can use today

Put together, the paper hands practitioners a field guide. To do offline RL by supervised learning, you do not need advantage weighting and you do not need a Transformer. A two-layer feedforward network trained simply to maximize likelihood is competitive with the state of the art, as long as you get two things right: tune the model's capacity and regularization carefully (grow the width until performance saturates, then add a little dropout if the dataset is small), and choose the right conditioning variable, trading off goals against rewards depending on the task.

The authors do not dodge the boundary of their result. On purely random data, TD learning still wins and RvS is clearly weaker, which they flag as an open problem for future work. For a reader, the value of the conclusion lies in that restraint: it does not claim supervised learning has solved offline RL, but tells you clearly when the simplest method is already good enough, and where it will fall short.

zh.text: 谈到离线强化学习（offline RL，只用一批预先收集好的数据、不与环境交互地学策略），大多数人的第一反应是价值函数：先学一个 Q 函数，再用它去改进策略。这类基于时序差分（TD, temporal-difference）的方法理论上很强，却出了名地难用，需要各种稳定化技巧和精细调参才能不发散。

于是有人换了个思路：把强化学习问题改写成一个「有条件的模仿学习」。核心洞察是，一条对某个目标来说很糟糕的轨迹，对另一个目标可能恰好是最优示范。只要给策略额外输入一个「想要达成的结果」，再用普通的监督学习去拟合数据里的动作，似乎就能绕开价值函数。但这条路线一直很模糊：不同论文给出了互相矛盾的结论，有的说必须做 advantage weighting（优势加权），有的干脆搬出大型 Transformer 序列模型。到底哪些组件是必需的，哪些只是额外的复杂度？

这篇发表于 ICLR 2022 的论文（作者来自 UC Berkeley 与 Carnegie Mellon）不打算再提一个新算法，而是把这些方法统一到一个框架下，称作 RvS（Reinforcement Learning via Supervised Learning，用监督学习做强化学习），然后用大量实验把它拆解到最简。结论出人意料：一个只有两层全连接的前馈网络（MLP），单纯地最大化似然，就能追平那些依赖 TD 学习或 Transformer 的最新方法。真正决定成败的，只有两件事，模型容量和「条件变量」的选择。

zh.caption: 图1 在 D4RL 的 Kitchen、Gym、AntMaze 三个套件上，条件于目标的 RvS-G（蓝）与条件于回报的 RvS-R（蓝）对比各类先前方法与基线。每根柱子是套件内多个任务的平均回报。仅凭一个前馈 MLP 的监督学习，RvS 就追平了使用 TD 学习和 Transformer 序列模型的方法。

zh.text: 论文链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.10751　　代码：https://github.com/scottemmons/rvs
为什么值得把方法「拆简」
基于价值的方法在离线和 off-policy 场景里长期占主导，也有漂亮的理论保证。但实际用起来门槛很高：要靠一堆技巧来稳定训练，还要小心调很多超参数。把 RL 转成有条件、过滤或加权的模仿学习，是一个诱人的替代方案，因为它只需要做监督学习。如果一个极简的监督学习配方真能追平这些复杂方法，那它对工程实践的意义就很直接：给从业者一份可靠的「操作手册」，同时也暴露出这类方法到底在哪里会失效。

论文的三点贡献可以这样概括。第一，它不发明新算法，而是把已有的目标条件（goal-conditioned）和回报条件（reward-conditioned）方法收进 RvS 这一个统一框架。第二，通过大规模实验把这些方法「蒸馏」到本质，证明一个两层 MLP 的最大似然训练就足以与最新方法竞争。第三，它明确指出哪些选择真正重要（模型容量、正则化、条件变量），并诚实地划出边界：在纯随机数据上，RvS 的表现明显弱于价值型方法，作者把它列为一个有待解决的开放问题。
RvS：一个刻意简单的框架

RvS 的设定很朴素。智能体处在一个马尔可夫决策过程中，我们训练一个「以结果为条件」的策略 π(a | s, ω)，其中结果 ω 可以是一个未来要到达的目标状态（对应 RvS-G），也可以是未来若干步的平均回报（对应 RvS-R）。给定一批离线轨迹，RvS 用「事后重标注」（hindsight relabeling）来构造训练集：轨迹里实际发生过的每个动作，都被当成「达成它后来真正达成的那个结果」的示范。

zh.caption: 图2 事后重标注示意：轨迹中的状态 s 与动作 a，被重新标注为通往它们实际到达的结果 ω 的示范。这样一来，一批未经筛选的经验就变成了「状态+目标 → 动作」的监督数据。

zh.text: 有了这样的数据，训练目标就只是最大化在条件策略下观测动作的对数似然：把结果 ω 拼接到输入状态 s 上，让一个两层全连接 MLP 去预测动作即可。这里没有 advantage weighting，没有 TD 自举，也没有 Transformer，只有一个在重标注经验上的最大似然目标。测试时，我们再给它指定想要的结果（一个目标状态或一个目标回报），让策略去执行。
在哪些任务上评测

评测覆盖面很广，横跨导航、运动控制和机械操作。在 D4RL 基准上用了三个套件：AntMaze（8 自由度四足机器人走迷宫）、Gym Locomotion（HalfCheetah、Hopper、Walker，数据质量从 random 到 medium-expert 不等）、以及 Franka Kitchen（9 自由度机械臂操作，由人类示范构成）。此外还用了 GCSL 套件里的目标条件任务，包括二维导航、Sawyer 机械臂、Lunar Lander 和机器爪；这些任务被改造成离线设置，数据由随机策略采集。所有分数都归一化到 [0, 100] 区间以便比较。

zh.caption: 图3 GCSL 套件中的几个目标条件环境（从左到右：FourRooms 导航、Lunar Lander、机器爪 Claw、开门 Door、推物 Pusher）。它们与 D4RL 的运动和操作任务一起，构成了从导航到精细操作的广谱评测。

zh.text: 结果：两层 MLP 就能达到当前最优

结论相当醒目。仅用一个两层前馈网络加最大似然训练，RvS 在多个套件上都达到了当前最优。在 AntMaze 上，目标条件的 RvS-G 平均得分 53.5，略微超过最强的价值型基线 CQL-p 的 50.6；在 Kitchen 上达到 54.0；在 GCSL 套件上得到 62.0，超过在线版 GCSL 的 58.0，而它用的还只是离线的随机策略数据。在 Gym Locomotion 上，回报条件的 RvS-R 追平了 Decision Transformer，却只用一个 MLP 而非大型 Transformer。

更反直觉的一点在于「子轨迹拼接」（subtrajectory stitching）。Kitchen 的 mixed 数据集和全部 AntMaze 任务，都需要把不同轨迹的片段拼起来才能完成，人们一直认为这类任务非得靠动态规划式的价值方法不可。但 RvS-G 在这里也能跟上，说明监督学习并不像想象中那样天然缺乏「拼接」能力。当然要如实说明：在 Gym 上价值型方法（如 CQL-r 的 63.0）仍然更高，RvS 的定位是「用最简手段追平」，而非全面碾压。

zh.caption: 表1 各套件归一化平均分（节选自论文表1，分数区间 [0, 100]）。
zh.note: 注：GCSL 一栏的 58.0 为在线 GCSL 方法。带 * 的部分基线在论文中使用 AntMaze v0 版本，细节见原文附录 A。RvS-G 未在以回报最大化表述的 Gym 上运行，故留空。

zh.text: 真正重要的两件事：容量与正则化

既然模型这么简单，成败就落在少数几个设计选择上。论文的消融实验把它们一一钉死。第一是容量：表现最好的网络比标准在线 RL 或模仿学习里用的要大，把隐藏层宽度一路加到 1024 通常都还在涨。第二是正则化：dropout 并非总是好的。它在小规模、由人类示范构成的 kitchen-complete 上能提升表现，却在 hopper-medium-expert 和 antmaze-medium-play 上反而有害。

zh.caption: 图4 容量与正则化的消融：在四个环境上改变网络宽度（横轴）与是否使用 dropout（蓝为无、橙为 p=0.1）。更大的网络在 hopper-medium-expert 和 kitchen-complete 上更好，印证了高容量策略网络的重要性；而 dropout 只在 kitchen-complete 这类小数据集上稳定有益。

zh.text: 一个自然的解释是：kitchen-complete 数据量小、又来自人类示范，更容易过拟合，所以需要 dropout 来正则化；而在数据更充足或本就偏随机的任务上，强行加 dropout 反而限制了策略容量。换句话说，高容量的策略网络与「恰到好处」的正则化要配合使用，才能拿到好结果。
第三个选择是策略的输出分布。论文比较了在离散化动作空间上的类别分布（categorical）与连续动作空间上的单峰高斯（Gaussian）。在 GCSL 套件里，类别分布总体上不逊于甚至优于单峰高斯，这又一次呼应了「更高的策略容量更有帮助」这一主线。此外还有一个提醒调参者的观察：验证损失与最终表现只是松散相关，因此它并不是一个可靠的调参信号。
把这三点合起来看，它们其实指向同一个方向：RvS 的成败主要取决于策略网络的表达能力，而不是某个花哨的训练技巧。容量要够大、正则化要因数据而异、输出分布要足够灵活，本质上都是在给这个简单的 MLP 更多拟合数据的自由度。这也解释了为什么不能只盯着验证损失去调参，论文观察到几组超参数设置的验证损失几乎相同，最终的评测回报却可能相差明显，说明真正起作用的因素并没有被验证损失完全捕捉到。

zh.caption: 图5 在 GCSL 套件的四个环境上，离散化动作空间的类别分布（橙）总体上匹配或超过连续动作空间的单峰高斯（蓝）。这与「更高容量的 RvS 模型表现更好」的整体规律一致。

zh.text: 一份可直接上手的操作手册

把这些拼起来，论文其实交出了一份从业者的「操作手册」：做离线 RL 的监督学习版本，你不需要 advantage weighting，也不需要 Transformer。一个两层前馈网络、单纯最大化似然，就能与当前最优竞争，前提是把两件事做对：一是仔细调好模型的容量与正则化（先把网络加宽到性能饱和，再视数据规模酌情加一点 dropout）；二是选对「条件变量」，也就是根据任务在目标（goal）与回报（reward）之间做取舍。
论文也没有回避它的边界。在纯随机数据上，TD 学习仍然占优，RvS 明显更弱，作者把这明确列为一个开放问题。对读者而言，这个结论的价值恰恰在于它的克制：它没有宣称监督学习「解决」了离线 RL，而是清楚地告诉你，在什么条件下最简单的方法就已经足够好，以及它会在哪里失手。

en.title: ICLR 2022: For Offline RL, a Two-Layer MLP Is All You Need
en.subtitle: Researchers at UC Berkeley and CMU strip "offline RL via supervised learning" down to its essentials, and find that only model capacity and the choice of conditioning variable really matter

这篇发表于 ICLR 2022 的论文（作者来自 UC Berkeley 与 Carnegie Mellon）不打算再提一个新算法，而是把这些方法统一到一个框架下，称作 RvS（Reinforcement Learning via Supervised Learning，用监督学习做强化学习），然后用大量实验把它拆解到最简。结论出人意料：一个只有两层全连接的前馈网络（MLP），单纯地最大化似然，就能追平那些依赖 TD 学习或 Transformer 的最新方法。真正决定成败的，只有两件事，模型容量和「条件变量」的选择。

en.title: ICLR 2022: For Offline RL, a Two-Layer MLP Is All You Need
en.subtitle: Researchers at UC Berkeley and CMU strip "offline RL via supervised learning" down to its essentials, and find that only model capacity and the choice of conditioning variable really matter

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 离线强化学习，其实一个两层 MLP 就够了
zh.subtitle: UC Berkeley 与 CMU 把「监督学习做离线 RL」拆到最简：真正重要的只有模型容量与「条件变量」的选择

en.caption: Figure 1. Across the D4RL Kitchen, Gym, and AntMaze suites, goal-conditioned RvS-G and reward-conditioned RvS-R are compared against prior methods and baselines. Each bar is the average return over many tasks in a suite. Using nothing but supervised learning with a feedforward MLP, RvS matches methods that rely on TD learning and Transformer sequence models.

en.text: Why bother stripping the method down

Value-based methods dominate offline and off-policy RL, and they come with attractive theoretical guarantees. In practice, though, they are hard to deploy: they require a stack of tricks to stabilize training and delicate tuning across many hyperparameters. Recasting RL as a conditional, filtered, or weighted imitation-learning problem is tempting precisely because it only asks for supervised learning. If a minimal supervised recipe can match the complex methods, it gives practitioners a dependable field guide, and it also reveals exactly where such methods still break down.

The paper's contributions come in three parts. First, rather than inventing a new algorithm, it places existing goal-conditioned and reward-conditioned methods under the single RvS framework. Second, through large-scale experiments it distills them to their essence, showing that a two-layer MLP trained with maximum likelihood is competitive with much more complex, state-of-the-art methods. Third, it pins down which choices genuinely matter (capacity, regularization, and the conditioning variable) and is honest about the limits: on purely random data, RvS is comparatively weak, a boundary the authors are careful to flag.

zh.caption: 图1 在 D4RL 的 Kitchen、Gym、AntMaze 三个套件上，条件于目标的 RvS-G（蓝）与条件于回报的 RvS-R（蓝）对比各类先前方法与基线。每根柱子是套件内多个任务的平均回报。仅凭一个前馈 MLP 的监督学习，RvS 就追平了使用 TD 学习和 Transformer 序列模型的方法。

zh.text: 为什么值得把方法「拆简」
基于价值的方法在离线和 off-policy 场景里长期占主导，也有漂亮的理论保证。但实际用起来门槛很高：要靠一堆技巧来稳定训练，还要小心调很多超参数。把 RL 转成有条件、过滤或加权的模仿学习，是一个诱人的替代方案，因为它只需要做监督学习。如果一个极简的监督学习配方真能追平这些复杂方法，那它对工程实践的意义就很直接：给从业者一份可靠的「操作手册」，同时也暴露出这类方法到底在哪里会失效。

论文的三点贡献可以这样概括。第一，它不发明新算法，而是把已有的目标条件（goal-conditioned）和回报条件（reward-conditioned）方法收进 RvS 这一个统一框架。第二，通过大规模实验把这些方法「蒸馏」到本质，证明一个两层 MLP 的最大似然训练就足以与最新方法竞争。第三，它明确指出哪些选择真正重要（模型容量、正则化、条件变量），并诚实地划出边界：在纯随机数据上，RvS 的表现明显弱于价值型方法，作者把它列为一个有待解决的开放问题。

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 离线强化学习，其实一个两层 MLP 就够了
zh.subtitle: UC Berkeley 与 CMU 把「监督学习做离线 RL」拆到最简：真正重要的只有模型容量与「条件变量」的选择

en.text: RvS: a deliberately simple framework

The setup is plain. An agent lives in a Markov decision process, and we train a policy conditioned on an outcome, π(a | s, ω), where the outcome ω can be a future goal state (giving RvS-G) or the average return over some future window (giving RvS-R). Given a batch of offline trajectories, RvS applies hindsight relabeling to build its training set: every action that actually occurred becomes a demonstration for whatever outcome that trajectory actually reached.

It helps to separate the two flavors of outcome. In RvS-G the outcome is a goal state, so the policy learns to reach configurations of the world; in RvS-R it is an average future return, so the policy learns to hit a level of performance. Hindsight relabeling is what makes both trainable from unlabeled logs: because we read off the outcome each action actually led to, even aimless or suboptimal experience becomes a valid demonstration for some outcome. That is the same insight that lets a trajectory which failed at one task serve as a perfectly good example for another.

en.caption: Figure 2. Hindsight relabeling. States s and actions a from a trajectory are relabeled as demonstrations toward the outcomes ω they actually reached, turning a batch of unfiltered experience into supervised (state + goal → action) data.

en.text: With that dataset in hand, the training objective is nothing more than maximizing the log-likelihood of the observed actions under the conditioned policy: concatenate the outcome ω onto the input state s, and let a two-layer fully connected MLP predict the action. There is no advantage weighting, no TD bootstrapping, and no Transformer, just a maximum-likelihood objective over relabeled experience. At test time you hand the policy the outcome you want (a goal state or a target return) and let it act.

zh.text: 在哪些任务上评测

评测覆盖面很广，横跨导航、运动控制和机械操作。在 D4RL 基准上用了三个套件：AntMaze（8 自由度四足机器人走迷宫）、Gym Locomotion（HalfCheetah、Hopper、Walker，数据质量从 random 到 medium-expert 不等）、以及 Franka Kitchen（9 自由度机械臂操作，由人类示范构成）。此外还用了 GCSL 套件里的目标条件任务，包括二维导航、Sawyer 机械臂、Lunar Lander 和机器爪；这些任务被改造成离线设置，数据由随机策略采集。所有分数都归一化到 [0, 100] 区间以便比较。

zh.caption: 图3 GCSL 套件中的几个目标条件环境（从左到右：FourRooms 导航、Lunar Lander、机器爪 Claw、开门 Door、推物 Pusher）。它们与 D4RL 的运动和操作任务一起，构成了从导航到精细操作的广谱评测。

en.title: ICLR 2022: For Offline RL, a Two-Layer MLP Is All You Need
en.subtitle: Researchers at UC Berkeley and CMU strip "offline RL via supervised learning" down to its essentials, and find that only model capacity and the choice of conditioning variable really matter

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 离线强化学习，其实一个两层 MLP 就够了
zh.subtitle: UC Berkeley 与 CMU 把「监督学习做离线 RL」拆到最简：真正重要的只有模型容量与「条件变量」的选择

en.text: What actually matters: capacity and regularization

Because the model is so simple, its success rests on a handful of design choices, and the ablations nail them down one by one. The first is capacity: the best architectures are larger than those used in standard online RL or imitation learning, and widening the hidden layers up to 1024 units generally keeps helping. The second is regularization: dropout is not universally good. It boosts performance on the small, human-demonstration kitchen-complete dataset, but it hurts on hopper-medium-expert and antmaze-medium-play.

en.caption: Figure 4. Capacity and regularization ablation across four environments, varying network width (x-axis) against dropout (blue = none, orange = p=0.1). Larger networks help on hopper-medium-expert and kitchen-complete, underscoring the value of high-capacity policy networks, while dropout is a reliable win only on small datasets like kitchen-complete.

en.text: One reading is that kitchen-complete is small and drawn from human demonstrations, so it is prone to overfitting and benefits from the extra regularization dropout provides, whereas on tasks with more data (or data that is already close to random) forcing dropout only throttles the policy's capacity. In other words, high-capacity policy networks and just-enough regularization have to be tuned together to get strong results.

The third choice is the policy's output distribution. The paper compares a categorical distribution over a discretized action space against a unimodal Gaussian over continuous actions. Across the GCSL suite, the categorical distribution generally matches or beats the Gaussian, echoing the same theme that more policy capacity helps. There is also a useful caution for anyone tuning these models: validation loss correlates only loosely with final performance, so it is not a reliable signal to tune against in practice.

en.caption: Figure 5. Across four GCSL environments, a categorical distribution over discretized actions (orange) generally matches or exceeds a unimodal Gaussian over continuous actions (blue), consistent with the broader pattern that higher-capacity RvS models perform better.

Put together, the paper hands practitioners a field guide. To do offline RL by supervised learning, you do not need advantage weighting and you do not need a Transformer. A two-layer feedforward network trained simply to maximize likelihood is competitive with the state of the art, as long as you get two things right: tune the model's capacity and regularization carefully (grow the width until performance saturates, then add a little dropout if the dataset is small), and choose the right conditioning variable, trading off goals against rewards depending on the task.

RvS：一个刻意简单的框架

RvS 的设定很朴素。智能体处在一个马尔可夫决策过程中，我们训练一个「以结果为条件」的策略 π(a | s, ω)，其中结果 ω 可以是一个未来要到达的目标状态（对应 RvS-G），也可以是未来若干步的平均回报（对应 RvS-R）。给定一批离线轨迹，RvS 用「事后重标注」（hindsight relabeling）来构造训练集：轨迹里实际发生过的每个动作，都被当成「达成它后来真正达成的那个结果」的示范。

zh.caption: 图2 事后重标注示意：轨迹中的状态 s 与动作 a，被重新标注为通往它们实际到达的结果 ω 的示范。这样一来，一批未经筛选的经验就变成了「状态+目标 → 动作」的监督数据。

zh.text: 有了这样的数据，训练目标就只是最大化在条件策略下观测动作的对数似然：把结果 ω 拼接到输入状态 s 上，让一个两层全连接 MLP 去预测动作即可。这里没有 advantage weighting，没有 TD 自举，也没有 Transformer，只有一个在重标注经验上的最大似然目标。测试时，我们再给它指定想要的结果（一个目标状态或一个目标回报），让策略去执行。

en.title: ICLR 2022: For Offline RL, a Two-Layer MLP Is All You Need
en.subtitle: Researchers at UC Berkeley and CMU strip "offline RL via supervised learning" down to its essentials, and find that only model capacity and the choice of conditioning variable really matter

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 离线强化学习，其实一个两层 MLP 就够了
zh.subtitle: UC Berkeley 与 CMU 把「监督学习做离线 RL」拆到最简：真正重要的只有模型容量与「条件变量」的选择

en.text: What actually matters: capacity and regularization

Because the model is so simple, its success rests on a handful of design choices, and the ablations nail them down one by one. The first is capacity: the best architectures are larger than those used in standard online RL or imitation learning, and widening the hidden layers up to 1024 units generally keeps helping. The second is regularization: dropout is not universally good. It boosts performance on the small, human-demonstration kitchen-complete dataset, but it hurts on hopper-medium-expert and antmaze-medium-play.

en.caption: Figure 4. Capacity and regularization ablation across four environments, varying network width (x-axis) against dropout (blue = none, orange = p=0.1). Larger networks help on hopper-medium-expert and kitchen-complete, underscoring the value of high-capacity policy networks, while dropout is a reliable win only on small datasets like kitchen-complete.

en.text: One reading is that kitchen-complete is small and drawn from human demonstrations, so it is prone to overfitting and benefits from the extra regularization dropout provides, whereas on tasks with more data (or data that is already close to random) forcing dropout only throttles the policy's capacity. In other words, high-capacity policy networks and just-enough regularization have to be tuned together to get strong results.

The third choice is the policy's output distribution. The paper compares a categorical distribution over a discretized action space against a unimodal Gaussian over continuous actions. Across the GCSL suite, the categorical distribution generally matches or beats the Gaussian, echoing the same theme that more policy capacity helps. There is also a useful caution for anyone tuning these models: validation loss correlates only loosely with final performance, so it is not a reliable signal to tune against in practice.

en.caption: Figure 5. Across four GCSL environments, a categorical distribution over discretized actions (orange) generally matches or exceeds a unimodal Gaussian over continuous actions (blue), consistent with the broader pattern that higher-capacity RvS models perform better.

zh.caption: 图4 容量与正则化的消融：在四个环境上改变网络宽度（横轴）与是否使用 dropout（蓝为无、橙为 p=0.1）。更大的网络在 hopper-medium-expert 和 kitchen-complete 上更好，印证了高容量策略网络的重要性；而 dropout 只在 kitchen-complete 这类小数据集上稳定有益。

zh.text: 为什么值得把方法「拆简」
基于价值的方法在离线和 off-policy 场景里长期占主导，也有漂亮的理论保证。但实际用起来门槛很高：要靠一堆技巧来稳定训练，还要小心调很多超参数。把 RL 转成有条件、过滤或加权的模仿学习，是一个诱人的替代方案，因为它只需要做监督学习。如果一个极简的监督学习配方真能追平这些复杂方法，那它对工程实践的意义就很直接：给从业者一份可靠的「操作手册」，同时也暴露出这类方法到底在哪里会失效。

论文的三点贡献可以这样概括。第一，它不发明新算法，而是把已有的目标条件（goal-conditioned）和回报条件（reward-conditioned）方法收进 RvS 这一个统一框架。第二，通过大规模实验把这些方法「蒸馏」到本质，证明一个两层 MLP 的最大似然训练就足以与最新方法竞争。第三，它明确指出哪些选择真正重要（模型容量、正则化、条件变量），并诚实地划出边界：在纯随机数据上，RvS 的表现明显弱于价值型方法，作者把它列为一个有待解决的开放问题。

en.subtitle: Researchers at UC Berkeley and CMU strip "offline RL via supervised learning" down to its essentials, and find that only model capacity and the choice of conditioning variable really matter

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 离线强化学习，其实一个两层 MLP 就够了
zh.subtitle: UC Berkeley 与 CMU 把「监督学习做离线 RL」拆到最简：真正重要的只有模型容量与「条件变量」的选择

en.caption: Figure 1. Across the D4RL Kitchen, Gym, and AntMaze suites, goal-conditioned RvS-G and reward-conditioned RvS-R are compared against prior methods and baselines. Each bar is the average return over many tasks in a suite. Using nothing but supervised learning with a feedforward MLP, RvS matches methods that rely on TD learning and Transformer sequence models.

en.text: The result: an MLP reaches state of the art

The headline is striking. Using only a two-layer feedforward network and a maximum-likelihood objective, RvS reaches state-of-the-art performance across several suites. On AntMaze, goal-conditioned RvS-G averages 53.5, edging out the strongest value-based baseline, CQL-p at 50.6. On Kitchen it reaches 54.0. On the GCSL suite it scores 62.0, beating online GCSL at 58.0, and it does so from purely offline, random-policy data. On Gym Locomotion, reward-conditioned RvS-R matches Decision Transformer while using a simple MLP rather than a large Transformer.

The most counterintuitive part concerns subtrajectory stitching. The mixed dataset in Kitchen and all of the AntMaze tasks require assembling fragments of different trajectories, and the field long assumed such tasks demanded dynamic-programming-style value methods. RvS-G keeps pace here too, which suggests that supervised learning is not as inherently incapable of stitching as one might expect. To be fair about the picture: on Gym, value-based methods (such as CQL-r at 63.0) still score higher, so RvS is best read as matching the state of the art with the simplest possible means, not as beating everything outright.

en.caption: Table 1. Normalized average scores per suite (excerpted from the paper's Table 1; scores in [0, 100]).
en.note: Note: the 58.0 in the GCSL row is the online GCSL method. Some baselines marked with * in the paper use AntMaze v0; see Appendix A of the original paper. RvS-G is not run on Gym, which is framed as reward maximization, so that cell is left blank.

zh.caption: 图1 在 D4RL 的 Kitchen、Gym、AntMaze 三个套件上，条件于目标的 RvS-G（蓝）与条件于回报的 RvS-R（蓝）对比各类先前方法与基线。每根柱子是套件内多个任务的平均回报。仅凭一个前馈 MLP 的监督学习，RvS 就追平了使用 TD 学习和 Transformer 序列模型的方法。

zh.text: 一份可直接上手的操作手册

把这些拼起来，论文其实交出了一份从业者的「操作手册」：做离线 RL 的监督学习版本，你不需要 advantage weighting，也不需要 Transformer。一个两层前馈网络、单纯最大化似然，就能与当前最优竞争，前提是把两件事做对：一是仔细调好模型的容量与正则化（先把网络加宽到性能饱和，再视数据规模酌情加一点 dropout）；二是选对「条件变量」，也就是根据任务在目标（goal）与回报（reward）之间做取舍。
论文也没有回避它的边界。在纯随机数据上，TD 学习仍然占优，RvS 明显更弱，作者把这明确列为一个开放问题。对读者而言，这个结论的价值恰恰在于它的克制：它没有宣称监督学习「解决」了离线 RL，而是清楚地告诉你，在什么条件下最简单的方法就已经足够好，以及它会在哪里失手。

zh.subtitle: UC Berkeley 与 CMU 把「监督学习做离线 RL」拆到最简：真正重要的只有模型容量与「条件变量」的选择

en.text: Ask most people how to do offline reinforcement learning, learning a policy from a fixed batch of logged data without ever interacting with the environment, and the answer usually starts with value functions: fit a Q-function, then improve the policy against it. Methods built on temporal-difference (TD) learning are powerful in theory, but they are notoriously fiddly in practice, leaning on stabilization tricks and careful hyperparameter tuning to keep from diverging.

An appealing alternative reframes the RL problem as conditional imitation learning. The key insight is that a trajectory that looks terrible for one goal may be an optimal demonstration for another. If you feed the policy an extra input, the outcome you want it to reach, and then simply fit the logged actions with ordinary supervised learning, you can sidestep value functions entirely. But the recipe had been murky. Different papers reached contradictory conclusions about what makes it work: some insisted on advantage weighting, others reached for large Transformer sequence models. Which components are actually essential, and which are just incidental complexity that a practitioner can safely drop?

This ICLR 2022 paper, from UC Berkeley and Carnegie Mellon, does not propose yet another algorithm. Instead it gathers these methods under one framework it calls RvS (Reinforcement Learning via Supervised Learning) and then, through extensive experiments, boils them down to the essentials. The finding is surprising: a plain two-layer feedforward network (an MLP), trained simply to maximize likelihood, matches the state of the art set by far more complex methods built on TD learning or Transformer sequence models. Only two things turn out to decide the outcome: how much capacity the model has, and what you condition on.

en.caption: Figure 1. Across the D4RL Kitchen, Gym, and AntMaze suites, goal-conditioned RvS-G and reward-conditioned RvS-R are compared against prior methods and baselines. Each bar is the average return over many tasks in a suite. Using nothing but supervised learning with a feedforward MLP, RvS matches methods that rely on TD learning and Transformer sequence models.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.10751　　Code: https://github.com/scottemmons/rvs
A field guide you can use today

Put together, the paper hands practitioners a field guide. To do offline RL by supervised learning, you do not need advantage weighting and you do not need a Transformer. A two-layer feedforward network trained simply to maximize likelihood is competitive with the state of the art, as long as you get two things right: tune the model's capacity and regularization carefully (grow the width until performance saturates, then add a little dropout if the dataset is small), and choose the right conditioning variable, trading off goals against rewards depending on the task.

The authors do not dodge the boundary of their result. On purely random data, TD learning still wins and RvS is clearly weaker, which they flag as an open problem for future work. For a reader, the value of the conclusion lies in that restraint: it does not claim supervised learning has solved offline RL, but tells you clearly when the simplest method is already good enough, and where it will fall short.

zh.text: 谈到离线强化学习（offline RL，只用一批预先收集好的数据、不与环境交互地学策略），大多数人的第一反应是价值函数：先学一个 Q 函数，再用它去改进策略。这类基于时序差分（TD, temporal-difference）的方法理论上很强，却出了名地难用，需要各种稳定化技巧和精细调参才能不发散。

于是有人换了个思路：把强化学习问题改写成一个「有条件的模仿学习」。核心洞察是，一条对某个目标来说很糟糕的轨迹，对另一个目标可能恰好是最优示范。只要给策略额外输入一个「想要达成的结果」，再用普通的监督学习去拟合数据里的动作，似乎就能绕开价值函数。但这条路线一直很模糊：不同论文给出了互相矛盾的结论，有的说必须做 advantage weighting（优势加权），有的干脆搬出大型 Transformer 序列模型。到底哪些组件是必需的，哪些只是额外的复杂度？

这篇发表于 ICLR 2022 的论文（作者来自 UC Berkeley 与 Carnegie Mellon）不打算再提一个新算法，而是把这些方法统一到一个框架下，称作 RvS（Reinforcement Learning via Supervised Learning，用监督学习做强化学习），然后用大量实验把它拆解到最简。结论出人意料：一个只有两层全连接的前馈网络（MLP），单纯地最大化似然，就能追平那些依赖 TD 学习或 Transformer 的最新方法。真正决定成败的，只有两件事，模型容量和「条件变量」的选择。
